topics.name: Variables and Expressions
topics.summary: A variable name is bound to an object. Reassignment changes that binding; it does not by itself modify or delete the previously bound object. Expressions can use values to calculate new results.

topics.name: Conditionals
topics.summary: Conditionals use Boolean conditions and comparisons to select which instructions execute based on specific cases.

topics.name: Loops
topics.summary: Loops repeat blocks of instructions using constructs like for and while, governed by indentation and state updates.

questions.question: What is the purpose of assignment in relation to a variable?
options: It binds a value to a variable name.
It deletes the variable from memory.
It prevents the variable from ever changing.
It transforms the variable into a conditional statement.
questions.explanation: Assignment binds a variable name to an object. Reassignment changes which object the name is bound to; it does not mean the old object itself was modified or deleted.

questions.question: What happens during reassignment to a variable?
options: The previous value is deleted permanently without replacement.
The variable name is bound to a new object.
A new independent variable is automatically created.
questions.explanation: Reassignment changes the object bound to the variable name. This alone does not imply that the previously bound object was modified or deleted.

questions.question: What can an expression do using stored values?
options: Terminate the execution of a program
Convert text into an unchangeable constant
questions.explanation: An expression can use stored values to calculate a new result.

questions.question: When does an if branch run?
questions.explanation: An if branch runs when its condition is true.

questions.question: In a simple if/else statement without elif, what is the role of the else branch?
options: It executes before the if branch is evaluated.
It handles the other case when the if condition is not met.
It restarts the current loop from the beginning.
It evaluates whether a variable should be reassigned.
questions.explanation: In a simple if/else statement without elif, the else branch handles the other case when the if condition is false.

questions.question: What do comparisons such as equality and greater-than produce?
questions.explanation: Comparisons such as equality and greater-than produce Boolean values.

questions.question: What does a for loop process?
questions.explanation: A for loop iterates over the elements provided by an iterable object.

questions.question: Unless exited early, under what condition does a while loop continue?
options: Exactly one time per sequence item
questions.explanation: A while loop repeats while its condition remains true. A break statement can exit the loop early.

questions.question: What determines which instructions belong to the loop body?
questions.explanation: Indentation determines which instructions belong to the loop body.
